missing: `--det-cache` (serial, no xdist needed) makes a passing order-dependent test FAIL: when a test that consumes in-process state left by earlier tests must rerun (one of its own inputs changed) while those earlier tests are reused (skipped), it runs without them. Plain and `--det` runs pass 5/5; the cached run reports 1 failed, and keeps failing on every later run (failures are never cached, the predecessors stay reused).
evidence: p/carry/test_c.py (work/PY2): record `pytest --det --det-cache=out/c` => 5 passed; `echo 2 > data.txt`; same command => "reused 4 ... ran 1 ... FAILED test_c.py::test_carried_state - assert 0 == 4"; `pytest -q` and `pytest -q --det` => 5 passed. Reproduced 2x. Carried-set rule only enters the key (crates/detpy-core/src/record.rs:874), nothing reruns the carried predecessors.

missing: Serial `--det` with pytest-xdist installed: xdist's `testrun_uid` fixture returns a fresh `uuid4()` every run (detpy derives it only under `-n`), the draw happens in xdist code which detpy treats as infrastructure, so it is neither controlled nor observed; `--det-cache` then records and reuses a test whose outcome depends on it (a coin-flip test cached as passed).
evidence: p/ent/test_e.py::test_uid_fixture (`assert testrun_uid[0] in "01234567"`): 3 `--det` runs => passed,failed,failed; `detpy verify` => "[outcome-only] identical observed events"; `--det-cache` run 1 recorded it, runs 2-7 receipts: {"nodeid":"test_e.py::test_uid_fixture","reused":true,"outcome":"passed"}. Cause: python/detpy/_sites.py:58 lists xdist as infra; xdist/plugin.py:407 `return uuid.uuid4().hex`.

missing: `--dist each` is not supported under `--det`: xdist's own scheduler runs (header says "not planned by detpy"), the merged trace keeps one record per test id although every test ran once per worker (40 runs, 20 trace records), and `--det-cache` records 40 entries and reuses 0 on every later run.
evidence: p/xd1: `pytest --det -n 2 --dist each --det-cache=out/cache.n2each` twice => both "reused 0 result(s) with proof, ran 40, recorded 40"; header "detpy: pytest-xdist --dist=each is not planned by detpy (xdist's own scheduling)"; python/detpy/xdist.py:79 `_UNSUPPORTED = {"each"}` (engine@claude/release-1).

missing: "Parallel with proof" is not enforced: `--det -n N` reports outcomes that differ from the serial `--det` run of the same suite (tests depending on process state of earlier tests, on the worker id, on the per-worker basetemp) and says nothing; the difference is only found if the user also runs serially and calls `detpy verify serial parallel` (class `placement`). Step P5 of docs/PARALLEL-PROOF-DESIGN.md (serial fingerprint per entry, serial-equivalent rerun) is not built.
evidence: p/xd2: `pytest --det` => 15 passed; `pytest --det -n 2` => 3 failed, 12 passed (no warning); `-n 4` => 5 failed; `detpy verify s.jsonl n2.jsonl n4.jsonl` => "covered 10 not covered 5 ... reasons: placement=5". docs/LIMITS.md O1: "nothing prevents it yet (P5 of the design)".

missing: The fixed plan is a function of the worker count: `-n 2`, `-n 3`, `-n 4` (and therefore `-n auto`/`-n logical` on runners with different CPU counts, and `--maxprocesses`) give different assignments and different outcomes for placement-dependent tests; a failure seen on an 8-core CI runner does not reproduce with `-n auto` on a 4-core laptop unless the user passes the CI's `.detpy/plan.json` with `--det-plan`. No message tells the user that `-n auto` resolved to a machine-dependent plan.
evidence: p/xd5: `--det -n 2` fails test_wid_fixture+test_uid_fixture (plan 2722af…), `-n 3` fails test_workercount (plan 34bf28…), `-n 4` fails test_wid_fixture+test_workercount (plan a72bae…); p/xd1: `-n auto` => "4 workers" plan 802209… vs `-n 2` plan 0fed63….

missing: `--det-cache` under `-n`: when any test reads the worker identity (worker_id fixture, PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER, per-worker basetemp) the second run re-plans, withdraws almost every reuse ("the plan moved a worker-id reader") and produces lopsided plans (12/3, 14/1, 1/13/2 tests per worker): the first warm run reuses 0 and the parallel speed-up is lost. The plan is not sticky to the plan that recorded the entries.
evidence: p/xd2: `pytest --det --det-cache=out/c2 -n 2` run 1 plan b64d87… (8/7), run 2 plan 07739c… "gw0=12/12, gw1=3/3 ... reused by the controller: 0; 12 reuse(s) withdrawn: the plan moved a worker-id reader ... not reused: env 1, new 3, placement 11"; p/xd5 `-n 3` 2nd time: "gw0=1/1, gw1=13/13, gw2=2/2 ... reused 0".

missing: `--det --det-cache -n N` gives different verdicts than `--det -n N` on the same code: the cache changes the plan (reused tests are removed, the rest is re-packed/quarantined), so placement-dependent tests move to other workers or lose their predecessors and flip. Same command, same code: 3 failed without the cache, 1 failed with a warm serial cache, 3 different failures after other `-n` values touched the cache.
evidence: p/xd2 with cache dir out/c1: serial record 15 passed; `--det --det-cache=out/c1 -n 2` => "1 failed, 14 passed" (test_carried_state assert 0 == 8); later same command => "3 failed" (test_wid_fixture gw1, test_wid_env, test_carried_state); `--det -n 2` without cache => always test_wid_env, test_carried_state (3 == 8), test_basetemp.

missing: A test that crashes its xdist worker has no record in the merged trace (only a `missing` marker): `detpy verify` of two such runs reports "missing: 0", every test covered, exit 0, so the crash is not a fingerprinted, comparable event and the crashed test cannot become a "reproducible defect" through the verifier.
evidence: p/xd3 (test_crash does os._exit(17)): `pytest --det -n 2` => "merged trace: 20 tests from 3 worker traces; MISSING 1 ... worker gw1 crashed in test_crash.py::test_crash"; `detpy verify out/c1.jsonl out/c2.jsonl` => "2 runs, 20 tests ... covered by Level 0: 20 not covered: 0 missing: 0" (21 tests ran).

missing: `--max-worker-restart=0` (or restart budget exhausted) under `--det -n`: the tests planned for the dead worker never run (fixed plan, no redistribution) and are only listed as MISSING in the merged trace; the session reports "1 failed, 11 passed" for a 21-test suite. Plain xdist behaves the same way, but the product promise of a complete deterministic run is not met and nothing reruns them.
evidence: p/xd3: `pytest -q --det -n 2 --max-worker-restart=0` => "merged trace: 11 tests from 2 worker traces; MISSING 10 ... 1 failed, 11 passed".

missing: Remote workers (`--tx ssh=...`, `--tx socket=...`, `--rsyncdir`) are not supported under `--det`: worker traces, cache shards, the barrier directory and the plan are side files under the controller's `<rootdir>/.detpy/` that a remote worker cannot write to the controller; the limit is only in docs, no usage error is raised.
evidence: docs/LIMITS.md O1 "Not supported: `--dist each` ..., remote `--tx` (side files under `.detpy/`), work stealing"; python/detpy/xdist.py:107 state_dir = <rootpath>/.detpy, :313 barrier under it; no check of the spec type in pytest_xdist_setupnodes (xdist.py:322). Could not run ssh here.

missing: `--dist worksteal` is accepted but silently replaced by a static plan (no stealing): the header only says "under a fixed plan (--dist=worksteal)"; with unknown or wrong durations (first run: every test weighs 1.0 s) an idle worker cannot take work from a loaded one, so the first run of a suite with uneven tests is slower than the customer's worksteal run.
evidence: p/xd1: `pytest --det -n 2 --dist worksteal` => "detpy: pytest-xdist under a fixed plan (--dist=worksteal) ... planned makespan 10.0s (LPT 10.0s)" (same plan digest 0fed63… as --dist load); docs/LIMITS.md O1 "Not supported: ... work stealing".
decide_for: Dynamic stealing is non-deterministic by nature; a fixed plan with recorded durations converges after one run.
decide_against: prefect and esphome integration tests use worksteal (DECLARED, PARALLEL-PROOF-DESIGN 1.1); the first run and every run after big duration changes is unbalanced, and the user is not told the mode was changed.

missing: A small anyio suite (asyncio + trio backends via the `anyio_backend` fixture) passes plain (18 passed in 1.0 s, together with pytest-asyncio and pytest-trio tests) but HANGS under `--det`: the run stops after the first test of test_anyio.py and is killed by `timeout 120`, twice in a row. By collection order the hanging test is `test_anyio_sleep[trio]` (`await anyio.sleep(0.1)` then `time.time() - t0 >= 0.1`); not isolated further (audit stopped), so the pytest-asyncio strict-mode and pytest-trio tests behind it were never reached under `--det`.
evidence: work/PY2/p/aio (venv async: pytest-asyncio, anyio, trio, pytest-trio): `./pp.py async aio strict -p no:cacheprovider` => "plain rc=0: 18 passed in 1.02s / det1 rc=124: test_anyio.py . / det2 rc=124: test_anyio.py ." ; logs p/aio/out/strict.det1.log, strict.det2.log.

missing: L1 does not exist on release-1 for Python: there is no `--det-threads` and no `--det-async` option (thread switches and asyncio event order are not controlled), although the brain records Block 3 as closed with `--det --det-threads` and ARCHITECTURE.md lists L1 as part of the engine. Only the event vocabulary (`Source::Sched`) is present in the core.
evidence: `pytest --help` in a venv with the release-1 wheel lists 30 `--det*` options, none of them threads/async (list in PY2.notes.md); `grep -rn "det-threads\|det-async\|det_threads\|det_async" python crates docs README.md` (engine@claude/release-1) matches only crates/detpy-core/src/verify.rs and event.rs. Brain DECISIONS.md 2026-11-18 "Block 3 (L1 threads) closed".

missing: No seeded asyncio scheduler on release-1 (`--det-async` absent): the order of ready callbacks, timers due together and executor completions is whatever the real loop does; docs/LIMITS.md C3 says asyncio keeps real time (`loop.time()` not virtualised). The L1 asyncio prototype lives only on `claude/l1-asyncio-study`.
evidence: Same grep as PY2-013; docs/LIMITS.md C3 "asyncio keeps real time: its selector blocks for real, so loop.time() is not virtualised"; brain ARCHITECTURE.md "L1 ... asyncio prototype built on claude/l1-asyncio-study".

missing: The order produced by `--det-seed=N` is a function of the selected item set: removing one test (`-k 'not uid'`, `--deselect`) reorders every other test of the module under the same seed, so a failing order found on the full suite cannot be narrowed with `-k`/`--deselect`/`--lf` and the same seed (only with `--det-order=FILE`).
evidence: p/xd1 `pytest --det --det-seed=5 --collect-only -q test_b.py` => b[0] wid b[1] b[2] b[4] b[5] uid b[3] env_wid; with `-k 'not uid'` => b[0] b[5] b[1] env_wid b[4] b[2] b[3] wid; with `--deselect 'test_b.py::test_b[0]'` => b[1] wid b[2] uid b[5] b[3] b[4] env_wid. python/detpy/plugin.py:862 shuffles the ids left after deselection.

missing: Under CI matrix sharding (`--splits/--group`, `--shard-id/--num-shards`, `--test-group-count/--test-group`) every shard gets its own shuffle of its own subset: the order inside a shard is not a subsequence of the unsharded seed order, and there is no shard-aware plan, merged trace or proof across shards (each shard is an unrelated session with its own order digest). A seed explored on the full suite at night does not describe what a shard runs; pytest-split's shard membership also depends on its `.test_durations` file.
evidence: p/xd1 venv split, `--det --det-seed=5`: full order "b[0] wid b[1] b[2] b[4] b[5] uid b[3] env_wid a[5] ..."; `--splits 2 --group 2` => "b[2] b[3] wid b[5] uid b[4] env_wid" (digest 874376…); `--shard-id=0 --num-shards=2` => "b[0] b[1] wid b[5] uid b[2] env_wid a[2] ..." (digest 9c631d…); full digest f7cda6….

missing: One uncontrolled entropy draw at import time of a conftest (e.g. `IMPORT_TOKEN = uuid.uuid4().hex`, a random database or bucket name) makes the whole suite uncacheable: 10 of 10 tests are refused on every run ("recorded 0"), including a test that does nothing; the only hint is the summary line "os entropy (not controlled; use --det-urandom)", it does not name the draw site.
evidence: p/ent2 (conftest.py line 2 draws uuid4 at import; test_first is `pass`): 8 runs of `pytest --det --det-cache=out/c` => every run "reused 0 result(s) with proof, ran 10, recorded 0 ... not cacheable: os entropy (not controlled; use --det-urandom) N, outcome M".

missing: By default `--det` does not control `os.urandom`, `uuid.uuid4`, `secrets`, `random.SystemRandom`: tests whose outcome depends on them still flip between identical `--det` runs (the verifier names the event, class `entropy`), so such a flaky test is not a reproducible defect and has no seed that makes it fail 10/10 unless the user adds `--det-urandom`.
evidence: p/ent/test_e.py, 3 runs of `pytest --det`: 1 failed / 2 failed / 3 failed (test_urandom failed,passed,failed; test_sysrandom passed,failed,failed); `detpy verify` => "reasons: entropy=4 outcome-only=1 ... event #0: os.urandom @ test_e.py:10 returned different values". docs/LIMITS.md R5.
decide_for: They are meant to be unpredictable; seeding them by default would weaken crypto tests (LIMITS R5).
decide_against: uuid4-named resources and token generation are a common flakiness source; promise 1 says every flaky test becomes reproducible; `--det-threads` already implied deterministic entropy on its branch (DECISIONS 2026-11-18).

missing: Under `--det -n N` nothing in the output says which tests are placement-sensitive or that the `--dist` scheduling was replaced beyond one header line; for `--dist no` combined with `-n 2` (xdist turns it into load) the header reports `--dist=load` without saying the option was changed.
evidence: p/xd1 `pytest --det -n 2 --dist no` => "detpy: pytest-xdist under a fixed plan (--dist=load); testrun_uid 491e55…" (plan digest identical to `-n 2`).
